1u05x67:468: In traditional web security, URL validation occurs before the request is sent. But at Agent runtime, "fetch this URL because someone asked for it" is itself normal product behavior — user-controlled or model-influenced URLs are the norm rather than the exception. This means the traditional validation paradigm fundamentally fails in Agent scenarios: DNS resolution at validation time may differ from the result at actual request time, and a domain that pointed to a public IP during validation may already point to the metadata endpoint by request time. OpenClaw's answer is to move the control point from "validation" to "egress". Proxyline, as a Node process-level routing layer, captures all outbound traffic and forces it through user-configured proxies — while policy enforcement happens at the proxy layer, not at the OpenClaw code layer. This is the design idea of "routing as enforcement", which is no different in essence from traditional firewalls enforcing policy at the network layer, just moved inside the process. The core value of this shift is: policy enforcement no longer depends on callers remembering to invoke validation logic; instead, traffic inevitably flows through the enforcement point.
